title: The Attack on the Chains
dek: The company stops the constructs battering a Chain, then struggles onward. Carmen catches up, pursuing flesh creatures force another fight, and making camp does not promise enough food or rest.

facts.Recorded dates: 29–30 Oct 2026 · quest source posts; one continuing expedition
facts.Setting: The Chains; ordered forest; Wasteland route toward the Maw; Voraketh
facts.People: Ithilrûnë Ailinor; Sildithas; Coralyn; Pappy; Carmen; Paco; Larcatelqui
facts.Outcome: The constructs and later pursuers fall; the company camps under the pull, still short of the Maw
facts.Latest continuation: 5 November 2026 · source posts resume the same march; a difficult camp follows

body:
The gongs came from enormous axes falling on a Chain. Ithilrûnë, Sildithas, Coralyn and Pappy answered an attack on the boundary they had previously struggled to approach.

Defeating the constructs would give them a chance to inspect the damage. They chose to go farther before their strength had fully returned, and the route toward the Maw began taking its own toll.

Stew under the falling trees

A gong woke the company in Voraketh. It sounded like metal striking metal, so low that the trees seemed to vibrate. Falling timber followed. Sildithas came out of their trance and called Larcatelqui. Ithilrûnë tried to work out whether the noise was moving. Coralyn immediately denied responsibility, then offered the stew the others had not eaten.

The meal and the alarm competed for their attention. Pappy would eat, while Ithilrûnë protested that this was not picnic time. Another gong brought a wave of force pulling toward the Chain and knocked her off her feet. She took to her broom; Sildithas rode ahead, leaving Coralyn and Pappy to hurry after on the ground.

From the air, Sildithas saw two enormous constructs alternately bringing axes down on the Chain. The usual problem had been guardians preventing an approach. These machines were attacking the boundary itself.

Trying to pull the fight away

Ithilrûnë wanted the attackers drawn away from the Chain. Its suppression limited the magic she could use. Sildithas went in before the others caught up, striking with a blade they had carried since Gael. The first blows rang against a defense too hard to penetrate; they withdrew by magic and tried again.

The constructs moved with surprising fluidity and came after the paladin and mount. Ithilrûnë recognized their kind from an earlier attempt to reach the center with Carmen, when they had been pursued instead. Recognition did not explain why these two were behaving differently.

Sildithas landed stronger, divinely charged strikes and tried to draw them onward. Ithilrûnë wondered from their color whether they were made of Delerium. Sildithas was unsure. The material and the identity of whoever sent them were still questions as the fight began.

The spell strikes the Chain too

Ithilrûnë brought down meteors filled with necrotic force. They hit the attackers, but a meteor also struck the Chain. Another gong rang out. The ground shook and the trees tilted toward the boundary, throwing Pappy, Sildithas and Coralyn down.

The opening in the constructs’ defenses still had to be used. Sildithas got up and pressed the attack. Coralyn struggled to close the distance; from farther back she could not reach everyone with her healing. She ran forward, protesting that she moved faster in water.

Ithilrûnë attacked again and backed away on her broom. One construct threw its axe at her while releasing a haze. Sildithas saw how badly she was hanging on and drove into the remaining threat with a cry for Physisia, life and chaos. Coralyn finally reached them with healing magic.

Both constructs fell and were reduced to dust. Ithilrûnë came down bleeding. Coralyn closed her wounds and admitted how frightening they had looked. The attack on the Chain had stopped; its damage was still there to examine.

Damage without a completed break

Sildithas put aside gathering materials and joined the inspection. Trying to combine divine healing with their contamination left them coughing. Pappy looked over the boundary, while Ithilrûnë examined the place the constructs had struck.

Her Guidance still failed. Despite the axe blows and necrotic impact, the Chain continued suppressing magic. The narrator described its magic as severely weakened rather than gone. Sildithas saw signs of necrotic energy across the contaminated metal.

Pappy noticed that this side had suffered badly in the plague, while the desolation beyond looked uniform, as though the infection had not survived there. Ithilrûnë suspected a weak point and a common force behind plague and attackers. The narrator supported the narrower finding that the plague had weakened this area of the Chain through an attack it had not been built to withstand.

That did not identify the constructs’ sender or prove every theory connecting the island’s crises. The company had stopped two machines and found a still-functioning, damaged boundary.

A choice made before they recover

Ithilrûnë wanted to continue toward the Maw before the next attack decided matters for them. Sildithas had the conviction to go, but could not promise the strength to survive. Coralyn could no longer repeat her greatest healing, though she offered a way to teleport them back if necessary. That escape remained a plan, not a tested return from the journey ahead.

They agreed to cross. Sildithas immediately lost their footing and began rolling under the pull. Pappy helped them up. Coralyn felt something leaving her and tried to keep her fear quiet. Ithilrûnë urged them onward.

Pappy thought they might have to fight, or perhaps he could speak to the presence as a druid. Those were hopes about an encounter they had not yet reached. The narrator warned that a route which had taken days in easier conditions would now be a long, difficult journey.

When the protection wears off

Ithilrûnë used Freedom of Movement and telekinesis to brace herself. The force slid around her. Coralyn worried about spending strength they might need in a fight, then used the same movement protection after another patch of ground tore free.

That earth struck Pappy in the back and sent him tumbling. Coralyn reached for him; he tried to anchor a hand axe in the ground and later thanked her for the help. Sildithas put on crampons. They gave some purchase on the soft stone, but each step took effort to plant and pull free.

An hour passed. The movement spells ended. Ithilrûnë lost her footing when the pull seized her again. The successful protection had been temporary, and it had not established a solution for everything the Wasteland could take from a traveler.

What Coralyn no longer remembers

Coralyn’s mind grew quieter. In the closing narration, she did not remember ever having used telepathy; she remembered only speaking aloud. That is a specific change in her recollection at this point, not proof that every ability or every other memory was permanently gone.

Sildithas encouraged the others to keep their spirits up. Coralyn asked them to be careful, still trying to walk without falling. They remained on the route, bracing against a pull that had already overturned people and torn up the ground.

At the packet’s cutoff, the two constructs are defeated and the Chain’s remaining function is established. The group has crossed into a harder journey, but has not reached the Maw in this continuation. No meeting, final explanation, safe return or complete recovery of what the travelers are losing is recorded yet.

Carmen catches up

Hours into the march, Carmen finally rejoins the company. Getting there has cost her a tumble under the same pull; Paco is thrown forward too before recovering. The narrator describes him briefly struggling to remember why he is there. Carmen complains about her hips and lateness rather than offering a grand entrance.

The group’s food does not last. Eating brings only temporary relief, and they keep reaching for provisions that are no longer there. Sildithas grows exhausted. When Carmen falls again, Coralyn reaches for her and Pappy catches her. Paco enlarges himself to carry her onward.

Theories about memory and order travel with them. Ithilrûnë suggests imposing memory on the Maw; Sildithas asks how that relates to the motes they have been carrying. Their discussion is an attempt to choose a course, not a demonstrated means of releasing the island.

They cannot walk away from everything

Four huge creatures of flesh feed on each other near the remains of a structure. Coralyn urges the others to pass quietly, comparing the danger to the Shadow Roads. For a while they move on. Then they notice the creatures following: not gaining ground, but not falling farther behind either. Stopping to rest would bring the danger to them.

Ithilrûnë asks Pappy and Sildithas to spend what strength they can now so the party keeps options later. Sildithas admits their reserves are low, prays, strengthens companions and attacks. Carmen blasts a wounded target down. Pappy joins the fight; Sildithas encourages him through another blow. When the final creature grabs Carmen, she burns it.

The company has survived the pursuit. Carmen finds motes in the remains, and Sildithas takes time to harvest something useful. Those gains do not answer the increasing hunger or make the next stretch easier.

Rest, while the ground still pulls

Ithilrûnë initially wants to get as far as possible, but the growing hunger and shaking legs change the decision. She asks for shelter and then proposes camp. Coralyn makes stew; Ithilrûnë and Pappy offer to watch. There is no nearby structure to shelter against.

Pappy judges that they cannot go much farther without people falling apart. Rest is necessary, but it is not secure recovery. He and Carmen struggle to lie comfortably while the pull threatens to throw them sideways. Ithilrûnë gets something to eat and still goes to sleep hungry. There is not enough for everyone. Coralyn offers part of her own bowl to Sildithas.

The scene closes before deciding every share or establishing that everyone benefits from rest. The company has reached a camp, not the Maw. Their inability to remember, eat or simply stop remains part of the journey still ahead.

People, places and connected histories Voraketh · Ithilrûnë Ailinor · Sildithas · Coralyn · Pappy
